todays_goal: Hold futur proche until Atticus reliably uses the correct aller form plus an infinitive.

lessons.subject: french
lessons.previous_learning: Day 19 showed the idea of futur proche is understood, but Atticus wrote wrong aller forms and changed infinitives: vous allez regarde for ils vont regarder, tu va lire, and je vais mange.
lessons.course_context: Oral-first mastery repair before adding new French grammar.
learning_objectives: Choose the correct aller form for the subject.
Keep the second verb in the infinitive.
Produce futur proche orally and in writing.
lessons.why_it_matters: The pattern must become automatic before longer French sentences are added.

vocabulary.definition: aller plus an infinitive to say what someone is going to do
the unchanged dictionary form of a verb

lessons.written_instruction: Atticus: futur proche has two parts: correct ALLER form + action verb in the infinitive. Example: Ils vont regarder.

worked_examples.title: Ils
worked_examples.explanation: Ils uses vont; regarder stays infinitive.

worked_examples.title: Tu
worked_examples.explanation: Tu uses vas; lire stays infinitive.

independent_practice.prompt: Translate: They are going to watch the match.
Translate: You are going to read. (tu)
Translate: I am going to eat.

exit_ticket.prompt: Say five new futur proche sentences without looking.
exit_ticket.answer: Correct aller form + infinitive in all five.

lessons.voice_prompt: Oral first. Give one English cue at a time. Require subject -> aller form -> infinitive. If the second verb is conjugated, say only: Keep the second verb in its dictionary form. Do not provide the full assigned sentence.
lessons.teacher_notes: Do not advance until 90%+ oral/written mastery.
